acts.25.p1.b1.text: Three days after his arrival in the province, Festus went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem, where the chief priests and Jewish leaders presented their case against Paul. They urged Festus

acts.25.p1.b2.text: … they were preparing an ambush to kill him along the way.

acts.25.p1.b3.text: “Paul is being held in Caesarea, and I myself am going there soon.

acts.25.p1.b4.text: When Paul arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around him, bringing many serious charges that they could not prove.

acts.25.p2.b5.text: “I have committed no offense against the law of the Jews or against the temple or against Caesar.”

acts.25.p2.b6.text: But Festus, wishing to do the Jews a favor, said to Paul,

acts.25.p2.b7.text: “Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem to stand trial before me on these charges?”

acts.25.p3.b8.text: “I am standing before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be tried.

acts.25.p3.b9.text: I have done nothing wrong to the Jews, as you yourself know very well.

acts.25.p3.b10.text: If, however, I am guilty of anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die.

acts.25.p3.b11.text: But if there is no truth to their accusations against me, no one has the right to hand me over to them. I appeal to Caesar!”

acts.25.p4.b12.text: Then Festus conferred with his council

acts.25.p4.b13.text: “You have appealed to Caesar. To Caesar you will go!”

acts.25.p4.b15.text: King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.

acts.25.p5.b16.text: “There is a certain man whom Felix left in prison.

acts.25.p5.b17.text: While I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and elders of the Jews presented their case and requested a judgment against him.

acts.25.p5.b18.text: “… it is not the Roman custom to hand a man over before he has had an opportunity to face his accusers and defend himself against their charges.

acts.25.p6.b19.text: “… I did not delay. The next day I sat on the judgment seat and ordered that the man be brought in.

acts.25.p6.b20.text: But when his accusers rose to speak, they did not charge him with any of the crimes I had expected.

acts.25.p6.b21.text: “… a certain Jesus who had died,

acts.25.p6.b22.text: but whom Paul affirmed to be alive.

acts.25.p7.b23.text: “Since I was at a loss as to how to investigate these matters,

acts.25.p7.b24.text: But when Paul appealed to be held over for the decision of the Emperor,

acts.25.p7.b25.text: “I would like to hear this man myself.”

acts.25.p8.b28.text: Agrippa and Bernice came with great pomp and entered the auditorium, along with the commanders and leading men of the city.

acts.25.p8.b29.text: And Festus ordered that Paul be brought in.

acts.25.p9.b30.text: “King Agrippa and all who are present with us, you see this man. …

acts.25.p9.b31.text: … he ought not to live any longer.

acts.25.p9.b32.text: “I have nothing definite to write to our sovereign one about him.

acts.25.p9.b33.text: For it seems unreasonable to me to send on a prisoner without specifying the charges against him.”
